Self-registration

Source: vignettes/self-registration.Rmd
self-registration.Rmd

By default appauth is a closed system: an administrator creates every user. Since 0.11.0 an application can also allow visitors to create their own accounts. All related settings are off by default, so upgrading an application or a database does not open registration by itself.

When to use it

Self-registration is appropriate when everyone with an approved email address may enter the application. If access must be granted one by one, keep the default and create users with aa_create_user().

Two paths are supported:

  • a Create an account link on the login form, with email confirmation;
  • Google sign-up: an account is created automatically after a Google sign-in if the verified email is not in the database.

The link appears only when the database already has users. On an empty database the first administrator is still created with the usual form, so registration cannot create the first administrator.

Settings 

settings <- aa_settings(
  registration_enabled = TRUE,
  registration_verify_email = TRUE,
  registration_role = "viewer",
  registration_domains = c("example.com"),
  registration_max_per_hour = 10,
  reset_enabled = TRUE,
  reset_base_url = "https://apps.example.com/my_app",
  send_reset = function(email, link, login) {
    # the application sends the email with emayili, telegram.bot, etc.
    message("Registration link for ", login, ": ", link)
  }
)
settings$registration_role
#> [1] "viewer"

registration_role must be one of roles and cannot be admin_role, so a visitor can never grant themselves administrative rights. registration_domains is optional; when set, only addresses in those domains can register. The hourly limit counts all pending requests, including requests that were never confirmed.

With registration_verify_email = TRUE (the default), send_reset and reset_base_url are required. The app calls send_reset(email, link, login); the link contains ?register=<token> and must be forwarded to the visitor. With FALSE the account is created immediately, which is sensible only in a controlled environment.

The confirmation token is one-time, has the same lifetime as a password reset link and is stored only as sha256. The password is hashed before it is stored in the pending registration. If someone creates the same login or email while the link is unused, confirmation fails instead of taking over the existing account.

The form response

The package deliberately returns the same answer whether or not the login and email were available. A request with an existing account does not reveal that fact on screen; the reason is written only to the on_event hook. This prevents enumerating users through the registration form.

Google sign-up 

settings <- aa_settings(
  google_enabled = TRUE,
  google_client_id = Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID"),
  google_client_secret = Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  google_redirect_uri = "https://apps.example.com/",
  google_domains = c("example.com"),
  google_signup = TRUE,
  registration_role = "viewer"
)

google_signup = TRUE requires google_enabled = TRUE. By default google_signup_require_domains = TRUE also requires a non-empty google_domains list: without it any Google account could create an account. Set that option to FALSE only for an intentionally open application.

The email is taken from the verified Google token. The login is the local part of the address with unsupported characters replaced by dots; a numeric suffix is added if the login is already taken. The new account gets a random password hash, so it can only be used through Google until an administrator sets a password. registration_domains does not apply here: the relevant domain check for Google sign-in is google_domains.

Events and cleanup

The hook receives registration_requested, registration_confirmed, registration_failed and google_user_created. A successful registration also emits login_success with the value registration, because the module signs the new user in. Tokens and passwords are never written to events. See aa_events() and the extension-points vignette.

aa_cleanup() removes expired and used registrations together with other stale tokens. It is called automatically by aa_session_connection(prepare = TRUE).

Logic without the module

Applications with a custom interface can call the exported functions directly:

result <- aa_register_user(
  conn, "ivan", "a-long-password", "ivan@example.com", settings
)
result$reason # "sent" or "created"

# after the visitor follows the link from the email
aa_registration_token_login(conn, token) # login or NULL
aa_confirm_registration(conn, token, settings) # creates the account

aa_register_user() returns the reason in a list; do not show user_exists or email_exists to a visitor. aa_confirm_registration() raises an appauth_error_user error when the link is invalid or the account data changed meanwhile.
